findings.cause: The rear legs are thick wedge slabs that go straight down and out from the shell. Under the body they make a solid red skirt (worst red is band 3, 8% of the sheet). The sheet has thin, separated legs there.
findings.fix: Make the leg5–8 upper prisms about 25% thinner so gaps open between the legs.

findings.cause: The front-left legs in the sheet arch up to a high knee, then drop and reach far to the left. The model's front legs are straight wedges that never rise above the shell rim, so the arched leg band on the upper left is uncovered.
findings.fix: Split each front leg into an upper segment that rises to a knee above the rim (around y 0.45) and a lower segment that drops. As a stopgap, rotate leg4.upper and leg1.upper so their tips point upward.

findings.cause: The head with its fangs sits low and forward in the sheet. In the model, head#2 is buried under the shell overhang, so the face and fangs barely read.
findings.fix: Move head#2 forward in z and enlarge it so it sticks out from under the shell.

findings.cause: Leg tips spread to z about ±0.4 and the wedges are wide. This makes the large red triangles at the front and back of the base. The sheet's legs gather under the body and are thin.
findings.fix: Thin the upper leg prisms and pull the lower prisms in along z.

findings.cause: The sheet has a large round dark abdomen bulging behind the shell. abdomen#0 (r 0.11) is too small to show.
findings.fix: Increase the abdomen radius by about 1.3x and move it back and down.

findings.cause: The upper legs are flat, broad wedges, about 0.08 wide and tapering wide at the root. The sheet shows thin legs, so red fills the area between them.
findings.fix: Lower the radius of all upper leg prisms.

findings.cause: Same fat leg roots, plus body#2 and body#6 are wide slabs that spill past the oval belly.
findings.fix: Thin the legs and narrow the underside slabs on x.

Move the head (head#2) forward to z≈0.32 and raise r to 0.13 so the face and fangs sit in front of the shell, as in the sheet.
